# Manuel Fas

> Machine learning researcher and engineer with experience across three research labs in Spain and Switzerland, specialising in Transformer architectures, NLP and large language models, and deep learning for sequential, tabular and biomedical data. Reimplements state-of-the-art papers into reproducible PyTorch codebases.

- Name: Manuel Fas (full name: Manuel Fas Ruiz)
- Location: Salamanca, Spain (open to international roles and relocation)
- Current role: Junior Machine Learning Researcher, BISITE Research Group (University of Salamanca), Salamanca, Spain, Sep 2026 – Present.
- Education: Dual B.S., Business Administration for Tech Companies and Computer Science, Pontifical University of Salamanca (UPSA), Sep 2022 – May 2027 (expected). Visiting Exchange Student, Computer Science, Lucerne University of Applied Sciences and Arts (HSLU), Sep 2025 – Jan 2026.
- Interests: Deep learning, Computer vision, Natural-language processing, Large language models (LLMs).
- Spoken languages: Spanish (native), English (professional working proficiency).

## Projects

- [Reimplementation of clickstream event sequence analysis model TRACE](https://fasmanuel2002.github.io/projects/trace-reimplementation/): Transformer-based user representation learned from attributed clickstream event sequences. Re-implements the TRACE architecture in PyTorch and evaluates it on alternative public e-commerce datasets, because the dataset used in the original TRACE paper is not publicly available. Result: 0.787 AUROC · 0.696 AUPRC for TRACE (multi-task), average over the ATC, SAT and MAP tasks on the OTTO dataset. Code: https://github.com/Fasmanuel2002/AAI_HSLU_TRACE. Research project report (PDF): https://fasmanuel2002.github.io/papers/TRACEPAPER_Report.pdf
- [Application of AI and Deep Learning to Genomic and Transcriptomic Data Analysis in Cancer](https://fasmanuel2002.github.io/projects/upsa-thesis-cancer-survival/): Bachelor's Thesis, Pontifical University of Salamanca (UPSA), July 2026. Application of AI and deep learning methods to genomic and transcriptomic data analysis in cancer. Data: TCGA breast cancer RNA-seq (RSEM) expression and clinical data from cBioPortal, study brca_tcga_pub2015 (Breast Invasive Carcinoma, TCGA, Cell 2015); 819 patients raw, 519 after preprocessing. Models: Cox Lasso, Cox Elastic Net, Random Survival Forest, DeepSurv, Cox-nnet. DeepSurv achieved the best discriminative performance (C-index of approximately 0.82). Code: https://github.com/Fasmanuel2002/UPSA_Thesis_Research. Thesis (PDF): https://fasmanuel2002.github.io/papers/TFG_ManuelFasRuiz.pdf
- [Paper-Reimplementations](https://fasmanuel2002.github.io/projects/paper-reimplementations/): PyTorch reimplementations of baseline and state-of-the-art machine learning and AI models. Code: https://github.com/Fasmanuel2002/Paper-Reimplementations. Papers:
  - 01 Sequence to Sequence Learning (Completed). Based on "Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks" (arXiv:1409.3215). PyTorch LSTM encoder-decoder baseline (weights initialized uniformly between -0.08 and 0.08, following the Seq2Seq paper) and a bidirectional-GRU encoder with additive (Bahdanau) attention, compared with BLEU and ROUGE.
  - 02 Attention Is All You Need (Completed). Based on "Attention Is All You Need" (arXiv:1706.03762). Decoder-only, GPT-style Transformer language model (about 11 million parameters) with token and positional embeddings, causal masked multi-head self-attention, feed-forward layers, layer normalization and residual connections, trained for next-token prediction on a dataset of William Shakespeare's works on an NVIDIA L4 GPU, following Andrej Karpathy's 'Let's build GPT: from scratch' tutorial.
  - 03 Predicting Issue Types with seBERT (Completed). Based on "Predicting Issue Types with seBERT" (arXiv:2205.01335). Fine-tunes a locally stored seBERT checkpoint (24-layer BERT encoder, hidden size 1024) with two binary heads, worth_automating and enough_information, on github-labels-annotated.csv using the Hugging Face Trainer.
  - 04 An Image Is Worth 16×16 Words (Completed). Based on "An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale" (arXiv:2010.11929). Encoder-only Vision Transformer in PyTorch: 16x16 patch embedding (224x224 images into 196 patches), learnable [CLS] token and position embeddings, pre-norm encoder blocks with multi-head self-attention and a GELU MLP; 12 layers, hidden size 384, MLP size 1536, 6 attention heads, about 21.5 million parameters; trained on an NVIDIA L4 GPU.
  - 05 Revisiting Deep Learning Models for Tabular Data (Planned/in progress). Based on "Revisiting Deep Learning Models for Tabular Data" (arXiv:2106.11959). Data preprocessing has started; there is no model yet.
  - 06 Switch Transformers (MoE) (Planned/in progress). Based on "Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models with Simple and Efficient Sparsity" (arXiv:2101.03961). The repository has no folder for this paper yet.
